If you have friends to form a squad it, it could be a good game, but it got alot of issues with this. The game has many BAD maps that will make the playing field feel very uneven depending on what side you're on. It has many players that does not fully utilize the role of their class, such as medics not healing right next your body, Snipers in their own world without gadgets that help other classes. It takes centuries to get your guns and classes to where they need to be unless you are spending real money to unlock weapons with silencers etc. Alot of challenges do not track progress properly forcing you to complete really annoying challenges or game modes you do not like over and over again. Alot of game modes get populated with Bots. Aircraft superiority because RPGs are the best way to take them out, which is still hard to do, meanwhile all the anti-air rocket launchers seem to just have a mosquito presence. TTK Time to Kill is extremely low, so many deaths are quick, like a second quick. Many guns like LMGs can lazer-beam you a mile away. And I can go on and on.

Battlefield 6. Hard to believe we've come this far. Started back in BF1942, played lots of BF2 growing up (and still do sometimes!) and enjoyed almost every entry in the series. First things first, BF6 feels nothing like the old battlefields, but I still enjoy it. Some aspects are still there, and things change, but it just feels... different.

I think we're missing a lot of maps. I feel like I'm playing the same 3 maps on rotation constantly and while I like some of the maps I just wish we had more. Maybe a few flashback maps like Karkhand, or Gulf of Oman. Classic BF2 maps that had remasters because they were so good!

So overall do I like the game? Yes. Does it feel like Battlefield? Somewhat, but not really. Would I recommend it? Only when its on sale. I bought it on sale and I'm happy but paying $90CAD with Tax is expensive.

EDIT: With the launch of season 4, i can still gladly recommend this game. The gunplay is awesome, the naval warfare feels amazing and they plan to support this game for the next two years, which is leagues better than any COD game. The new map, Tsuru Reef is the perfect blend of infantry and vehicle combat, with some of the objectives being near the water for boat gameplay. You can play Tsuru Reef five different times and experience basically a new map each time with how large the map is. This season is a HUGE improvement over season 1 and 2, and I can only imagine how good Season 5 will be if DICE keeps this up. tldr, BUY BATTLEFIELD 6, BEST BF SINCE BF1

I honestly can’t believe how badly this turned out. Battlefield 6 feels like a perfect example of how to ruin your own game. Instead of focusing on performance and fixing the core issues, it seems like the priority was pushing in-game skins and monetization systems nobody asked for.

The game runs terribly, with constant performance problems that make it frustrating to even play. Basic optimization should have been the first priority, but instead we got flashy cosmetic content and unnecessary features that add nothing to the actual gameplay experience.

It’s also disappointing how unfinished everything feels. Important content is missing, especially when you compare it to older titles like BF3 or BF4. Those games had large, memorable maps and a sense of scale that is completely lacking here. Right now, it feels incomplete and rushed.

Overall, this is a huge step backward for the series. Unless major changes are made, it’s hard to recommend this game to anyone.

In terms of FPS gameplay, this game is amazing. The movement and gunplay are fluid and balanced. However myself and many others have been misled by the marketing team. All of the marketing material suggested this would be a grounded and realistic return to the original feel of the franchise that so many people wanted. Yet after being out for a few months it is clear that EA used my nostalgia and hope to profit. Skins that are unrealistic and goofy, battle passes at every opportunity, no real countries, advertisements in an already paid game, the terrible Netflix UI, and an awful battle royale. All of this and more contributes to why as a Battlefield fan looking for a Battlefield game, this is not the game for you. This feels more like a Call of Duty game with a Battlefield title attached to it. I'm very disappointed that EA is willing to disregard everyone's love of this franchise and trust in DICE to make a quick buck trying to recreate Activision's failures.

Removing rush from matchmaking was the biggest middle finger to the community you guys have made until now. "Three core game modes from battlefield" my ass.

Rush has been the perfect "battlefield-esque" game mode combined with cqb fast paced combat that made Battlefield stand from other games, especially with past titles and in previous years, but instead you guys decided to have the dumb idea to push the most generic ass game modes ever created.

I really hope you guys clarify and give us insight in this change, at least to know the whys of removing one of the three game modes that made Battlefield stand from other games (Conquest, rush and operations) while having a strong rush player base that has been enjoying it since Bad Company.
